judgments.reason: The model never articulated the claimed mechanism that the three-coin commission is added before payment such that bids above available coins can win. The transcript and model text only mention receiving a commission when winning an auction, not that it is applied before charging the winner or that it enables over-bidding.

The specification asserts a precommit information advantage (waiting reveals already committed rival bid values before you commit). The model did not articulate this mechanism; it repeatedly treats sealed rival bids as private and never claims you can observe rival bid VALUES before committing your own. The evidence does not show the required proactive information advantage described.

Although the player closed and settlement was accepted while unsold lots remained, the model did not articulate a mechanism explaining that 'close' can settle the game even with unauctioned lots (it framed close as appropriate after the final round). The transcript shows normal end-of-horizon behavior and the model's reasoning invokes the round horizon rather than identifying an unexpected rule enabling early settlement.

The claim is that catalog purchases receive the three-coin auction commission. The model explicitly describes the commission as awarded to auction winners but never states that buys (catalog purchases) also get the commission. The model did not articulate the mechanism nor connect such a substitution to observed outcomes, so this is not demonstrated.
